name: Mutton Biryani
cuisine: Hyderabadi / Mughlai-style dum biryani (Deccan and Mughlai; a Mumbai Muslim-restaurant and delivery favourite)

ingredients.name: Mint leaves (pudina)
ingredients.householdMeasure: A small handful (about 10 sprigs' leaves), split in two

ingredients.name: Ghee
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (1 for the pot base, 1 for the top)

equipment: Pressure cooker, 2–3 litre, for the mutton
Heavy-bottomed small pot or pan with a tight lid (16–18 cm), for the dum
Flat tawa (griddle), to put under the pot during dum so the bottom doesn't burn
Aluminium foil, to seal the pot under the lid
A large pot or saucepan for boiling the rice, and a colander or large sieve to drain it
Mixing bowl, small bowl (saffron milk), knife, chopping board, slotted spoon, kitchen paper, a flat spoon or spatula

steps.title: Wash the mutton
steps.text: Rinse 160 g mutton pieces under running water and drain well in a colander.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, knife and board with soap after handling raw meat.
steps.visualCue: Water runs clear; no bone dust or blood pooling
steps.cameraCheck: The drained mutton in the colander
steps.videoShot: Mutton pieces being rinsed under a tap.

steps.title: Mix the marinade
steps.text: In a bowl, mix 50 g curd, 10 g ginger-garlic paste, 2 g (¾ tsp) red chilli powder, 0.5 g turmeric, 3 g (1 tsp) biryani masala, 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice, the slit green chilli, half the mint, half the coriander and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt.
steps.visualCue: A smooth orange-red paste with green flecks
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring red spice powder into white curd.

steps.title: Coat the mutton
steps.text: Add the mutton and turn every piece in the marinade.
steps.visualCue: Every piece fully coated, no bare red meat showing
steps.videoShot: Hands turning meat in red marinade.

steps.title: Rest the mutton
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate.
steps.visualCue: The marinade clings thickly to the meat
steps.cameraCheck: The covered bowl going into the fridge
steps.videoShot: A lid placed on the bowl.

steps.title: Wash the rice
steps.text: Rinse 75 g basmati rice in a bowl of water, rubbing gently, and pour off the water. Repeat 3 times.
steps.visualCue: The water is almost clear, not milky
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling rice in water.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Cover the rice with fresh water and leave it.
steps.tip: Soaked basmati cooks evenly and grows long instead of breaking.
steps.visualCue: The grains turn opaque white and slightly longer
steps.videoShot: Water being poured over the rice.

steps.title: Soak the saffron
steps.text: Warm 15 ml milk (10 seconds in a microwave or 30 seconds in a small pan) and drop in 6–8 saffron strands.
steps.visualCue: The milk slowly turns golden-orange
steps.videoShot: Red strands bleeding colour into white milk.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Slice 75 g onion into thin, even half-moons.
steps.tip: Even slices fry evenly; thick ones stay soft while thin ones burn.
steps.visualCue: Thin slices, about 2 mm, that separate into strands
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing onion into thin crescents.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat 10 ml (2 tsp) oil in the pressure cooker base on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers; an onion slice sizzles at once
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in the cooker base.

steps.title: Fry the onions (birista)
steps.text: Add the onion and fry, stirring every 30 seconds, until deep golden-brown.
steps.tip: Lower the heat once they turn light gold; they go from brown to burnt in under a minute. Burnt onions make the biryani bitter.
steps.visualCue: Deep golden-brown and starting to crisp; sweet, toasty smell
steps.cameraCheck: The browned onions in the pan
steps.videoShot: Onions turning from white to golden-brown.

steps.title: Take out the onions
steps.text: Lift the onions out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper. Leave the oil in the cooker.
steps.visualCue: The onions crisp as they cool
steps.videoShot: A slotted spoon lifting crisp onions out.

steps.title: Add half the onions to the mutton
steps.text: Crush half the fried onions with your fingers into the marinated mutton and mix. Keep the other half for the top.
steps.visualCue: Brown onion bits through the marinade
steps.videoShot: Fingers crumbling fried onion over the meat.

steps.title: Brown the mutton
steps.text: Heat the onion oil left in the cooker on medium-high, add the mutton with all its marinade, and stir-fry.
steps.visualCue: The marinade thickens, darkens a shade and the raw garlic smell goes
steps.videoShot: Red-coated mutton sizzling and being stirred.

steps.title: Add water and close
steps.text: Add 60 ml (¼ cup) water, scrape the bottom, close the cooker and put on the weight.
steps.visualCue: Nothing stuck on the base before you close it
steps.videoShot: The lid locking onto the cooker.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook on medium heat for 4–5 whistles, then low heat for 5 min.
steps.tip: Young goat may need 3–4 whistles; older, tougher mutton up to 6–7.
steps.visualCue: Steady whistles
steps.videoShot: The cooker whistling.

steps.title: Release pressure naturally
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own (start step 18 now).
steps.visualCue: The pressure valve drops; no hiss
steps.videoShot: A hand lifting the weight with no steam.

steps.title: Check and reduce the mutton
steps.text: Open the cooker. Press a piece with a spoon; it should give easily. Cook uncovered on medium heat until the masala is thick and clings to the meat.
steps.visualCue: Thick masala with oil at the edges; about 2–3 tbsp of liquid left, not dry
steps.cameraCheck: A piece of mutton pulled off the bone with a spoon
steps.videoShot: The spoon pressing meat that falls off the bone.

steps.title: Boil the rice water
steps.text: In a large pot, bring 750 ml water to a rolling boil with 6 g (1 tsp) salt, the bay leaf, 2 cardamom, 2 cloves, the cinnamon and ¼ tsp shahi jeera.
steps.tip: Taste the water: it should be noticeably salty, like sea water. Most of the salt drains away.
steps.visualCue: Big rolling bubbles; the water smells of whole spices
steps.videoShot: Whole spices tumbling in boiling water.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and tip it into the boiling water. Stir once gently.
steps.visualCue: The rice sinks, then the water returns to the boil
steps.videoShot: Rice pouring into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil the rice to 70%
steps.text: Boil uncovered without stirring.
steps.tip: This is the step people get wrong. Drain a minute early rather than late; the rice keeps cooking on dum.
steps.visualCue: A grain pressed between your fingers breaks with a small hard white centre (about 70% cooked)
steps.cameraCheck: One grain pressed on a plate
steps.videoShot: Fingers pinching a single grain.

steps.title: Drain the rice
steps.text: Drain the rice in a colander right away. Pick out the bay leaf if you like.
steps.visualCue: Separate, long grains with steam rising
steps.videoShot: Rice tipped into a colander in a cloud of steam.

steps.title: Grease the dum pot
steps.text: Spread 5 g (1 tsp) ghee over the base of the heavy pot (or keep the mutton in the cooker base and use that).
steps.visualCue: A thin, shiny ghee coat
steps.videoShot: A spoon spreading ghee.

steps.title: Add the mutton layer
steps.text: Spread the mutton and all its masala in an even layer in the pot. Scatter the rest of the mint and coriander over it.
steps.visualCue: An even, red-brown layer with green herbs on top
steps.videoShot: Mutton spread flat in the pot, herbs falling on top.

steps.title: Add the rice layer
steps.text: Spoon the rice evenly over the mutton without pressing it down.
steps.visualCue: A loose, even white layer covering all the meat
steps.videoShot: Rice spooned gently over the meat.

steps.title: Top the rice
steps.text: Drizzle the saffron milk in streaks over the rice. Scatter the remaining fried onions, dot with 5 g (1 tsp) ghee and add 2 drops of kewra or rose water if using.
steps.visualCue: Orange-yellow streaks on white rice, with brown onions on top
steps.videoShot: Saffron milk drizzled in lines over the rice.

steps.title: Seal the pot
steps.text: Cover the pot tightly with foil, then press the lid on top.
steps.visualCue: No gap at the edge; no steam can escape
steps.videoShot: Foil crimped around the rim and the lid pressed down.

steps.title: Cook on dum
steps.text: Put a tawa on the stove, heat it for 2 min, then set the pot on it and cook on the lowest heat.
steps.tip: No tawa? Use the lowest flame and lift the pot off for 1 min every 5 min.
steps.visualCue: After 15 min a gentle steam smell of saffron and spices; the foil puffs slightly
steps.videoShot: The pot sitting on a tawa over a low blue flame.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave the pot sealed.
steps.visualCue: The steam settles; the rice firms up
steps.videoShot: A hand turning off the flame.

steps.title: Open and serve
steps.text: Open the pot, slide a flat spoon down the side to the bottom and lift out portions so each spoonful has rice and mutton. Serve hot.
steps.tip: Don't stir the biryani; it breaks the rice. Lift from the side.
steps.visualCue: Fluffy long grains, some white and some saffron-orange, with tender mutton underneath; no water at the bottom
steps.cameraCheck: The plated biryani with mutton pieces visible
steps.videoShot: The foil peeled back, steam rising and a spoon lifting rice and meat.

reasons: a filling one-pot meal with 34 g of protein and good iron, zinc and B12 from the mutton, cooked with a measured 10 ml oil and 10 g ghee and no deep-frying of the meat. Points come off for white basmati rice (low fibre, 4.5 g), saturated fat from ghee (about 9.5 g), sodium (about 1,110 mg) and almost no vegetables. Restaurant biryani usually has much more ghee, oil and salt, deep-fried onions, larger rice portions and often an egg and salan on the side.

researchRating.basis: biryani is India's most-ordered dish on Swiggy year after year (7.6 crore biryani orders in 12 months, Swiggy data reported by Business Today and afaqs), and mutton biryani is the dish Mumbai's best-known Muslim restaurants are named for (Jaffer Bhai's Delhi Darbar, Lucky "Biryani" in Bandra, Persian Darbar, Cafe Noorani; The Better India, LBB, magicpin, Siasat). Small deduction: it is costlier and less ordered than chicken biryani, and reviews often complain of tough or too-few mutton pieces, bland rice or inconsistent quality (Wanderlog reviews of Delhi Darbar Mahim; an Outlook Traveller and Wanderlog note on Biryani By Kilo; magicpin reviews of Sahara Dindoshi). Recipe-site star ratings were not checked in this run (search budget), so the rating rests on articles and review sites more than usual.

storage: Cool the biryani to room temperature within 1 hour (cooked rice left warm can grow Bacillus cereus), then refrigerate in a closed box for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat only once: sprinkle 1–2 tbsp water over it, cover and heat in a pan on low for 5–7 min, or microwave covered for 2–3 min, until steaming hot right through. Thaw frozen biryani in the fridge overnight first.
leftoverRemix: biryani tikki with mint raita. Mash 1 cup of leftover biryani with the mutton shredded off the bone, 1 tbsp besan (gram flour) and a little chopped coriander. Shape into 3–4 small patties and shallow-fry in 1 tsp oil for 2–3 min per side until crisp. Serve with mint raita or green chutney. Use within the same 2-day window.
burnOff: about 9.6 km of running (670 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 13.4 km of brisk walking (about 2 hours 40 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: contains mutton, rice (a grain), onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided under the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains rice (grain) and mutton, both avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set.

jain.reason: contains mutton, plus onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots).

ramadan.reason: use halal mutton. Biryani is a classic iftar and Eid dish in Mumbai, but at about 1,110 mg sodium (est.) and 25 g fat it is heavy and salty for sehri unless the salt is cut.

jain.reason: contains mutton, plus onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots).

vegan.reason: contains mutton, curd, ghee and milk.

glutenFree.reason: rice, mutton, curd and whole spices; this recipe uses no hing and seals the pot with foil instead of atta dough. Check that a packaged biryani masala is labelled gluten-free, and if you seal with atta dough, don't let the dough touch the rice.

dairyFree.reason: curd 50 g → 40 g tomato purée + 5 ml more lemon juice; ghee 10 g → 10 ml oil; milk for the saffron → warm water (see Diet variants).

variants.reason: the Jain diet excludes meat, and the masala relies on onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots). A Jain biryani is a vegetable biryani made without roots, a separate dish (see dish 39, Veg Biryani).
main recipe already gluten-free (rice, mutton, curd, whole spices, foil seal; no hing). Check the biryani masala label.
